findings.claim: The profile's website text goes stale after the user edits the website in preferences, and stays wrong until a full page reload. The old client-computed websiteName followed model.website. The new server-only model.website_name is never refreshed on the client. Results: changing the website shows the old name; adding a website to an empty profile shows no globe or link; clearing it still shows the old name.
findings.evidence: User#save (models/user.js.es6 ~166-215, 204-213) copies only bio_excerpt from the PUT response and ignores data.user.website_name. preferences.js.es6:117-123 refreshes only name and bio_cooked. routes/preferences.js.es6:6 reuses modelFor('user'). routes/user.js.es6:51-54 runs findDetails only in afterModel on entering the user route, not when moving between child routes. All three seats reasoned this; none ran it.
findings.reason: Accepted regression, raised independently by both correctness seats and mattpocock. Unverified so far: before fixing, make it red with an acceptance test (edit the website in preferences, save, visit the summary, assert the link text and presence). Fix direction: set website_name from the PUT response or re-run findDetails after save. If it cannot be made red, defer it as unverified and keep it Important.

findings.claim: include_website_name is dead code because it lacks the trailing '?'. website_name is therefore always serialized, as null when there is no website.
findings.evidence: Gemfile.lock:22 pins active_model_serializers 0.8.3, which only calls include_<attr>?. Every other filter in the file has the '?' (include_email? :117, include_card_image_badge_id? :161, include_stats?), and so do 99 definitions across app/serializers. No caller of the '?'-less name exists.
findings.reason: All four seats agree, and the evidence is a concrete library-version citation. Minor, so no red test is required, but a spec asserting website_name is absent for a blank website would guard it.

findings.claim: The website-is-a-subdomain-of-instance case (website www.example.com, instance example.com) is not treated as same domain and shows only the host. The reverse case (website example.com, instance forum.example.com) shows the full path, so the matching is asymmetric.
findings.evidence: The host has 3 labels and the instance 2, so the else branch runs. "example.com".ends_with?(".www.example.com") is false. superpowers gave a reasoned spec: stub current_hostname 'example.com', website 'http://www.example.com/u', and json[:website_name] is 'www.example.com', not 'www.example.com/u'.
findings.reason: Accepted: it misses the PR's stated rule in its most common case. superpowers' proposed spec serves as the red test.

findings.claim: The sibling-subdomain branch compares everything after the first label, so unrelated sites on a shared public suffix are treated as the same domain and show the full path. Examples: evil.co.uk vs forum.co.uk, a.github.io vs forum.github.io, hosted *.trydiscourse.com.
findings.evidence: Lines 143-146 match any two hosts with the same label count (>2) and equal labels after the first. The seats agree the impact is cosmetic: the shown text is the real, HTML-escaped URL.
findings.reason: Accepted: it breaks the stated 'same as instance domain' rule. Minor UX only, not spoofing.

findings.claim: The host comparison is case-sensitive, so http://Example.com/u does not match instance example.com.
findings.evidence: Ruby URI#host keeps the original case, and the comparison does not normalise it. Reasoned, not run.
findings.reason: Accepted. Downcase both hosts before comparing; a mixed-case spec makes it red.

findings.claim: The sibling-subdomain branch (www.example.com vs forum.example.com) has no spec, and it is the most complex branch and the one carrying the over-match bug.
findings.evidence: spec lines 76-91 cover only exact match, different domain, and website-is-parent-of-instance.
findings.reason: Accepted. CONTRIBUTING.md says 'Include tests'. Add a spec for this branch, including a negative public-suffix case.

findings.claim: No spec covers a missing or blank website, including that website_name is absent or nil in that case.
findings.evidence: spec lines 76-91 have no blank-website case. open-code-review notes such a spec would have caught the dead include_website_name filter.
findings.reason: Accepted. Add a blank-website spec; it also guards the include filter fix.

findings.claim: website_name is not in untrusted_attributes. When scope.restrict_user_fields?(object) is true, website is hidden but website_name (host and possibly full path) is still sent, leaking a restricted user's website.
findings.evidence: The untrusted_attributes list (lines 25-33, 105-111) generates include_<attr>? with a presence check and the restrict_user_fields? check. :website is on the list and :website_name (declared at :43) is not. Reasoned by ponytail and flagged as outside its lane.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by one advisory seat only, so it is not reported or fixed in this loop. Severity normalised up to Important because it is a privacy leak. Unverified; it would be settled by a serializer spec with restrict_user_fields? stubbed true, asserting website_name is absent. Recommend a fresh verifier.

findings.claim: The displayed 'complete URL path' drops the query string and fragment (http://example.com/u?id=1 shows example.com/u).
findings.evidence: Only URI#path is appended. The seat notes this may be intended.
findings.reason: Appendix: one seat only. Possibly intended behaviour.

findings.claim: A port is silently dropped when the path is shown (example.com:8080/u displays as example.com/u).
findings.evidence: host + path omits URI#port.
findings.reason: Appendix: one seat only.

findings.claim: A same-domain URL whose path is '/' now renders with a trailing slash as example.com/.
findings.evidence: host + URI#path where the path is '/'.
findings.reason: Appendix: one seat only.

findings.claim: An unrelated change rides along (the @property doc tag corrected from websiteName to profileBackground), against CONTRIBUTING.md's 'one feature or bug-fix per branch'.
findings.evidence: The one-line doc change at models/user.js.es6:59 is unrelated to the PR title.
findings.reason: Appendix: one seat only. Other seats call the change harmless, but none disproves the convention breach.

findings.claim: Documentation fix: the @property name changed from websiteName to profileBackground.
findings.evidence: The seat's own report says the change is correct and has no risk.
findings.reason: Not a defect: the raising seat's report states the change is correct and has no risk, and open-code-review independently lists it as 'doc-comment fix only'.

findings.evidence: spec lines 76-91 have no invalid-URI case.
findings.reason: Appendix: two seats.

findings.claim: No spec covers the 'same label count but different domain' path.
findings.evidence: spec lines 76-91 do not exercise it.
findings.reason: Appendix: one seat only.

findings.claim: No spec covers the reverse subdomain case (website www.example.com on instance example.com).
findings.evidence: spec lines 76-91 cover only website-is-parent-of-instance.
findings.reason: Appendix: one seat only. The main-list asymmetry fix's red spec would cover it.

findings.claim: No acceptance or integration test covers moving the website-name logic from a client computed property to a server field.
findings.evidence: No test covers the client-side refresh behaviour after a preferences save.
findings.reason: Appendix: one seat only. The red acceptance test required for the main-list stale-website finding would close it.

findings.claim: website_name re-parses URI(website.to_s) in each branch and repeats discourse_host.split('.').
findings.evidence: host + URI(website.to_s).path is built at :141, :146 and :149, and split('.') is called three to four times.
findings.reason: Appendix: two seats. Advisory duplication or over-engineering.

findings.claim: The three-branch if/elsif/else with nested ternaries is a single boolean written the long way. The branches never overlap and can flatten to one OR with the same behaviour.
findings.evidence: Every branch yields either host or host + path. With equal label counts, ends_with?('.host') implies equal hosts, which branch 1 already handles. ponytail supplied an ~8-line equivalent.
findings.reason: Appendix: one advisory seat only. Optional cleanup.

findings.claim: The in-place append '"." << website_host' makes readers stop to check for mutation; '"." + website_host' or interpolation is clearer.
findings.evidence: Line 149. mattpocock and open-code-review both note it is functionally fine without frozen_string_literal, which does not dispute the readability claim.
findings.reason: Appendix: one advisory seat only. Readability nit.

coverage: Files skipped: none. All four seats reviewed all 5 files in the patch (controllers/user.js.es6, models/user.js.es6, templates/user/user.hbs, app/serializers/user_serializer.rb, spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb). open-code-review's tool excluded the two .es6 files and the spec, but the seat reviewed them manually. Axes that did not run: (1) the gate was not run (benchmark mode), so the review is unanchored with no executed ground truth; (2) no seat executed anything: no Ruby in the environment, no specs or JS run, no browser check of the Ember behaviour, so every finding is reasoned; (3) there is no spec, so spec compliance was measured only against the commit title; (4) no cross-family reviewer seat was used; (5) mattpocock did not check whether other clients (user card, admin) need website_name, beyond a grep finding only user.hbs. Standards docs were available and used: CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/TESTING.md, .editorconfig, .jshintrc.
